topic.angle: What open source allows, with Linux as the famous example

card.title: Open source means you can read the code

body.claim: Open-source software has publicly available source code that anyone may use, study, modify and share.
body.why: That is the definition, usually granted through an open licence. Linux is a family of free and open-source operating systems built on the Linux kernel, first released by Linus Torvalds on 17 September 1991. It is one of the most prominent examples of free and open-source collaboration.

probes.question: What does open source allow users to do with the code?
options: Use, study, modify and distribute it

probes.question: True or false: the Linux kernel was first released in 1991 by Linus Torvalds.
